elastic/kibana#910101.title: [Detection Engine] Run ES|QL rules when some source indices are missing
elastic/kibana#910101.body:
## Summary
Today an ES|QL rule fails the whole execution when one index in its `FROM` clause does not exist. Rules that query several sources stop alerting when one source is removed.

The rule executor should run the query on the indices that exist, record a warning in the execution log that names the missing indices, and set the rule status to `Partial failure` so the rule details page shows it.

## Acceptance criteria
- A rule whose `FROM` clause includes a missing index still runs on the existing indices and creates alerts.
- The execution log has a warning listing the missing indices.
- The rule details page shows `Partial failure` with the warning text.
- When every index in `FROM` is missing, the execution fails as today.

comments.author: pm-b
comments.body:
Scope update after the design review on 2026-11-04. Notes first, the decision for this issue is at the end.

Attendees: design, the Investigations PM, two engineers from the team and one from the data quality group.

Options we went through:
1. Ship the export flyout as written above, with CSV and NDJSON, the field picker and the 10,000 event cap. Design liked the flow, but the field picker needs the new field list component, which will not land before the next minor.
2. Ship CSV only, without the field picker, exporting the columns currently shown in the timeline. Smaller, but support asked twice for NDJSON so that exports can be loaded back into an index, so CSV alone would be revisited soon.
3. Split the work: keep the export behavior in one issue and track the setting that turns it on in another, so that the setting can ship first and the export later behind it.

Concerns raised: the 10,000 event cap is lower than the alerts table export, which confuses users who use both; the file name should include the timeline title and the time range; and the export must respect the field-level security of the user who runs it, which the current query helper does not do yet.

**Decision for this issue:** option 3. The export flyout and its acceptance criteria move to a new issue owned by the data quality group, and this issue now only adds the advanced setting that turns timeline export on, off by default.

elastic/kibana#913802.title: Saved query picker forgets the selected query after a page refresh
elastic/kibana#913802.body:
## Steps to reproduce
1. Open a timeline and pick a saved query from the query bar picker.
2. Refresh the page.

## Current behavior
The query bar still shows the query text, but the picker shows `No saved query` and `Update query` is disabled.

## Expected behavior
The picker keeps the selected saved query after a refresh.
